title.narrative: Area‐based, multi‐sectoral programming in Aldein, Barh Alarab, and Adila localities in East Darfur State

description.narrative: ltpgtThis project in East Darfur is strategically designed to address the urgent and pressing issue of acute malnutrition, with a particular focus on Severe Acute Malnutrition (SAM) in Bahar Alarab locality. Recognizing the gravity of the emergency, the project adopts a comprehensive approach to deliver Community Management of Acute Malnutrition (CMAM) services for the targeted population, including boys and girls.ltbrgtThe ambitious targets of the project aim to provide treatment for 575 individuals, coupled with a broader outreach to an additional 1,236 individuals through various initiatives. These include mother support groups, awareness sessions, and capacity-building programs for Ministry of Health (MOH) staff, community volunteers, and Community-Based Organizations (CBOs). Crucially, community participation is central to the project, involving the target communities in every stage, from needs identification to planning, implementation, and ongoing monitoring to ensure both effectiveness and sustainability. Additionally mothers-to-mothers (m-2-m) groups play a crucial role in empowering mothers and tackling nutritional issues, with a special emphasis on promoting Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices. The initiative underscores the importance of coordination with relevant sectors for multi-sectoral nutrition activities.ltbrgtThe primary goal is to save the lives of acutely malnourished children under five in diverse settings, including refugees, internally displaced persons (IDP), and host communities.ltbrgtBeyond nutrition-focused efforts, the project extends its reach to provide medical treatment for 15,000 individuals within the broader 4,919,462 targeted by the Health sector. Coordination efforts involve collaboration with the Health sector, Ministry of Health (MoH), and various service providers, aligning strategies with the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP) for 2024.ltbrgtIn addition to essential health and nutrition services, the project takes a holistic approach by delivering multi-services that combine health, nutrition, and Gender-Based Violence (GBV) interventions. This includes leveraging well-established Primary Health Care (PHC) facilities in Bahr Alarab locality and establishing a Women's Safe Space in Al Dein locality. The GBV intervention in Al Dein encompasses rehabilitating a women's center, establishing Community-Based Protection Committees, and providing training and awareness activities. with a target of 9,335, the key components of the GBV intervention involve case management, psychosocial support, distribution of dignity kits, and vocational training for women survivors. Capacity-building initiatives, including workshops on GBV in emergencies and the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), are integral to the project. Emphasis is placed on accountability.lt/pgtltpgtConflict sensitivity will be addressed in the project by conducting a thorough analysis of the conflict context, identifying and assessing risks and vulnerabilities in conflict-affected communities, engage with affected communities to understand their perspectives, needs, and priorities related to the conflict. ensure that interventions do not exacerbate conflict dynamics or increase risks, foster collaboration and coordination between humanitarian actors, government agencies, civil society organizations, and local communities, build the capacity of service providers and advocate for policies and practices.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgt
